decisions.quote: While in those instances the coefficients match after exponentiating, many of the credible intervals (CrI) still don’t match – we are not sure why that is. The differences are small and don’t affect the claims made by the authors, but they go beyond what could be explained by rounding error.
decisions.reason: Although the main substantive claims held, Axis 1 evaluates whether the original reported numbers were recovered; the authors explicitly report that many credible intervals (as well as some reported point estimates in Table 2) could not be recovered and differed beyond rounding error, which matches 'computational issues'.

parent_objection: First reply treats any CI difference beyond rounding as computational issues. Exact axis1 codebook allows rounding AND negligible numerical differences, and issues when discrepancies are treated as substantive. Source computational section says ultimately all reproducibility criteria fulfilled; coefficients match after exponentiating; CI differences small and do not affect claims; Conclusion says main findings reproduced successfully and issues minor. Settle whether these differences qualify as negligible numerical differences under exact codebook or substantive failure to recover central numbers. Read full computational section, Conclusion, and Table2; do not silently equate beyond-rounding with substantive. Outcome_robustness is separate. Return requested axis with shortest sufficient contiguous quote.

shipped.outcome_quote: Computational: While in those instances the coefficients match after exponentiating, many of the credible intervals (CrI) still don’t match – we are not sure why that is. The differences are small and don’t affect the claims made by the authors, but they go beyond what could be explained by rounding error. || Robustness: As a robustness check, we tried to reproduce the main findings of this paper using a frequentist modelling approach. We used logistic regression mixed models and included all the variables used by the authors, except for geographic relatedness. Results can be found in the replication table. Overall, the results from the frequentist models are very similar to the results from the Bayesian models and do not change the interpretation advanced by the authors (see Table 2).
